status_summary: No cap or phase-down was found. DOL issued an interim final rule on 2025-10-02 changing how H-2A wage rates are set (using BLS data in place of the discontinued USDA farm labor survey), citing labor shortage and food-supply concerns, and on 2026-08-03 published updated H-2A adverse effect wage rates under that methodology; the notice still describes the 2025 rule as interim, so no final rule was found. On 2026-02-03 DHS and DOL jointly published a temporary final rule (91 FR 5040) making up to 64,716 supplemental H-2B visas available for FY2026 on top of the 66,000 statutory limit, under authority extended by Public Law 119-37 (signed 2025-11-12) from Public Law 118-47; the visas are split into three allocations, mostly for returning workers early in the season, and are limited to employers attesting to permanent and severe financial loss. No supplemental rule for FY2027 was found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-13. Both actions keep or expand the programs, which runs opposite to the Mandate's recommendation to cap and reduce them; the Mandate also records alternative conservative views favoring the programs. On 2026-08-26 the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of California held four features of the 2025 H-2A wage interim final rule unlawful without vacating it and ordered DOL to issue a new methodology, and a DOL notice of 2026-09-02 says the current rates remain in effect pending new ones. These wage-setting rulings concern how rates are calculated, not the size of the program.

timeline.event: A federal court in Louisiana enters final judgment vacating DOL's 2023 H-2A wage-rate rule (Teche Vermilion Sugar Cane Growers v. Su), returning the program to the 2010 methodology, according to DOL's later rule.

DOL publishes an interim final rule, effective immediately, setting H-2A adverse effect wage rates for non-range occupations from BLS wage data by skill level instead of USDA survey data. DOL cites a claimed labor shortage tied to reduced illegal immigration and the end of the USDA survey; 887 comments were received by 2025-12-01. DOL reports H-2A worker requests rose from about 286,900 (FY2020) to about 391,600 (FY2024).

DHS and DOL jointly publish a temporary final rule (91 FR 5040, effective 2026-01-30 through 2026-09-30) making up to 64,716 supplemental H-2B visas available for FY2026 above the 66,000 statutory limit, under authority in Public Law 119-37 (signed 2025-11-12) extending Public Law 118-47; the visas come in three allocations, the first two for returning workers, and employers must attest to permanent and severe financial loss without the workers.

DOL's Employment and Training Administration publishes updated H-2A adverse effect wage rates for non-range occupations (91 FR 48946) under the methodology of the 2025-10-02 interim final rule, using BLS wage data released 2026-05-15 that represent May 2025 estimates (average rate 15.96 dollars), effective 2026-08-03, or 2026-08-17 for entities covered by the court order in Kansas et al. v. Department of Labor; the notice still describes the 2025 rule as interim.

In United Farm Workers v. Department of Labor (E.D. Cal., No. 1:25-cv-01614-KES-EGC), the court rules on summary judgment (order dated 2026-08-25, filed 2026-08-26) that four features of DOL's 2025 H-2A wage interim final rule were arbitrary and capricious (the two skill tiers, the housing adjustment, the use of OEWS data and the more-than-50-percent occupation-code rule). It holds the rule unlawful but does not vacate it for now, orders DOL to develop a new methodology and publish new wage rates promptly, retains jurisdiction, directs DOL to notify the public within seven days that employers may owe wage adjustments if workers were paid below the new rates, and reserves whether and how much back pay is due.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court, E.D. Cal. (copy of the filed order hosted on envoyglobal.com)

timeline.event: DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification posts a notice implementing the court order: current H-2A wage rates stay in effect until new ones issue, employers who use H-2A labor from 2026-09-02 until new rates are published may owe wage adjustments if workers are paid below the new rates, no payment obligation exists at this time, and DOL states it disagrees that back wages can be imposed and is considering further litigation and rulemaking.

title: Cap and phase down the H-2A and H-2B temporary worker visa programs
uncertainties: The FY2026 H-2B supplemental rule was read on 2026-10-13 (first 100,000 of about 106,000 characters): joint DHS and DOL temporary final rule, 91 FR 5040, up to 64,716 visas, authority from Public Law 119-37 extending Public Law 118-47; this resolves the earlier uncertainty about the visa number and issuing agencies. A Federal Register search for H-2B documents from 2026-02-04 to 2026-10-13 showed no FY2027 supplemental rule (only information collection notices), but FY2027 supplemental authority and any rule could still appear after that date or not be indexed under that term. The H-2A rule remains interim as of the 2026-08-03 notice; the court order in Kansas et al. v. Department of Labor, which the notice mentions for the effective date, was not examined. The effect of the H-2A wage change on wage levels was not verified and no characterization is made. A DOL proposed rule of 2026-03-27 on prevailing wages concerns H-1B, E-3 and PERM, not H-2A or H-2B (the visible text). Congressional bills to cap H-2A or H-2B were not searched. 'Diverged' reflects that the H-2B limit was raised, the opposite of the Mandate's cap; the H-2A action is a different design and not a direct reversal. Checked 2026-10-14: a Federal Register query for H-2A documents from 2026-08-04 and for H-2B documents from 2026-02-04 returned no final H-2A wage rule, no new H-2A wage notice and no FY2027 H-2B supplemental cap rule; a web search for FY2027 H-2B supplemental visas returned only FY2025 and FY2026 coverage. The court order was read from a copy hosted on envoyglobal.com; the reviewer confirmed on 2026-10-14 that it is the filed order itself (ECF header Document 99, filed 2026-08-26, 28 pages, signed 2026-08-25), not a summary. The order's introduction says the interim rule issued in August 2025 while its background section and citation give 2025-10-02; the Federal Register date is used. The judge's name does not appear in the copy read, and no appeal by DOL was found; DOL's 2026-09-02 notice says it is considering next steps in the litigation and rulemaking. No bill to cap H-2A or H-2B and no agency action narrowing either program was found, so the diverged call stands.
